hints: Look closely at the combination $\text{N s}^{2}\text{ m}^{-1}$ and recall how the newton $\text{N}$ breaks into base units $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$.
Replace $\text{N}$ by $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ inside $\text{N s}^{2}\text{ m}^{-1}$ so you can cancel powers of metres and seconds.
Simplify to a single base unit and check which of acceleration, force, mass and momentum is measured in that unit.
walkthrough: Start from the definition of the newton from $F = ma$: $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg} \times 1 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, so $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
Substitute this into the given units: $1 \text{ N s}^{2}\text{ m}^{-1} = (1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}) \times (1 \text{ s}^{2}) \times (1 \text{ m}^{-1})$.
The combination simplifies to $\text{kg}$, which is the SI base unit of mass, whereas force is $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, momentum is $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ and acceleration is $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
Therefore the quantity with units of $\text{N s}^{2}\text{ m}^{-1}$ is mass. This is option C.

options.A: Acceleration has units of $\text{m s}^{-2}$, which does not match $\text{N s}^{2}\text{ m}^{-1}$ when expressed in base units.
options.B: Force has units of $\text{N}$, equivalent to $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, so it lacks the extra $\text{s}^{2}\text{ m}^{-1}$ factor.
options.C: Substituting $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$ gives $\text{kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{s}^{2}\text{ m}^{-1} = \text{kg}$, the unit of mass.
options.D: Momentum has units of $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ or $\text{N s}$, which still contains $\text{m}$ and only $\text{s}$ to power 1.
